1.2 Music (yue) is that which arises from music (yin). 61
Its root
lies in the touching off of mens' hearts by [external] things.
for he whose heart is touched off to happiness,
his sound is spacious and leisurely
for he whose heart is touched off to joy,
his sound is expansive and far- reaching;

for he whose heart is touched off to anger, his sound is coarse and unyielding; for he whose heart is touched off to reverence, his sound is straightforward and upright; for he whose heart is touched off to love, his sound is harmonious and gentle. These six are not [inner] nature -- they are set in motion only after being touched off by things.62 For this reason, the former kings were cautious in what was used to touch them off (the people). Thus Ritual (li 4) was used to direct their wills,
Music (yue) was used to harmonize their voices (sheng),
Administration (zheng) was used to unify their actions,
and Punishment (xing JfIJ) was used to prevent their violations.
Ritual, Music, Punishment, and Administration --
their ends are one:
they are that which is used to unify the people's hearts and put forth the Way of Governance.
All music (yin) arises in the hearts of men.
Emotion is stirred within
and thus takes shape in sound (sheng).
Sound forms patterns,
and this is called music (yin).
For this reason,
the music of a [well-] governed age is peaceful,
so as to express happiness in the harmony of the administration.
The music of a chaotic age is resentful,
so as to express anger over the perverseness of the administration.
The music of a lost state is mournful,
so as to express thoughtfulness over the hardships of the people.
The Way of sound and music

connects with administration.64 [Zheng Xuan says: "This talks of how whether or not the eight timbres (yin) are in harmony depends upon the administration [of the state]. The 'Yu Zao' [chapter of the Li Ji] says: 'The blind musician in attendance judged whether the music were too high or low."'65]
1.4 Gong is the ruler,
shang is the minister,
jue is the people,
zhi is the affairs,
and yu is the things [of production].
If these five are not chaotic,
then there will be no discordant music (yin).
If the gong [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is disorganized,
[indicating that] the ruler is arrogant.
If the shang [tone] is chaotic,
If the jue [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is depressed,
[indicating that] the people are resentful.
If the zhi [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is mournful,
[indicating that] the affairs are overburdening.
If the yu [tone] is chaotic, then [the music] is precipitous,
[indicating that] the wealth [of the state] is depleted.
If these five are all chaotic,
and transgress upon each other in turn,
this is called "man" (dissolute) [music].
If it is like this,

then the extermination and passing away of the state will occur in no time at all. [Zheng Xuan says: "'The five' refer to the ruler, minister, people, affairs, and things. In all cases of tones (sheng), the lower (zhuo W, literally 'murky') ones are revered and the higher (qing q清, literally 'clear') ones are lowly.68 Zhanchi Mt M. is the appearance of being broken down (bibai, 敝敗) and unharmonious. If the ways of the ruler, minister, people, or things are chaotic, then their [corresponding] tones (yin) will be chaotic in response. Huang 荒 is like san 散 (scattered). Bi RI is qing 傾 (inclined, slanted). The [Shang] Shu says, "Wang... mao huang... 王耄荒）69 The Yi Jing says: "Wu ping bu bi (無平不陂), "there is no leveling that will not slant").70]
1.5 The music of Zheng and Wei
is the music of a chaotic age.
It borders on dissoluteness (man 漫).
The music from among the mulberries atop the Pu River
is the music of a lost state.
The administration was disorganized
and the people dispersed.

Superiors were slandered and private ends were carried out, and it could not be stopped. [Zheng Xuan says: "Bi t is like tong i- (to be the same as). [Among] the lands above the River Pu there was a Sangjian -- it is from these waters that the music of a lost country came out. In ancient times, Zhou of the Yin Dynasty made Shi Yan compose some licentious music. After a short while, he drowned himself in the River Pu. Later, Shi Juan passed by there, and at night heard [the music] and wrote it down. He played it for Duke Ping of Jin. This is the story it refers to. Sangjian is south of Puyang. Wu ~ means wang M (to accuse unjustly)."]
1.6 All music (yin)
arises in the hearts of men.
Music (yue)
is that which connects with [ethical] human relationships and principles (lunli).
For this reason,
those who know sounds (sheng) but do not know music (yin) --
these are the birds and the beasts.
Those who know music (yin) yet do not know Music (yue) --
these are the common masses.
Only the superior man (junzi) can know Music (yue).
For this reason,
sounds (sheng) are investigated to know music (yin),
music is investigated to know Music (yue),
Music is investigated to know administration,
and the Way of Governance is complete.
For this reason,
those who do not know sounds (sheng) can not be spoken with about music (yin);
those who do not know music can not be spoken with about Music (yue).
To know Music (yue)
is to be close to Ritual (li).
If Ritual and Music are both attained to (de 4),
this is called "having virtue (de ,)."
"Virtue" (de 4,), means "attainment" (de 4).
For this reason,
the prospering of Music (yue) [at the sacrifice]
is not [a matter of] reaching the extreme in music (yin);
the Ritual of the communal ancestral sacrifice
is not [a matter of] extending to the utmost in flavors.
The se in the Temple to King Wen (qingmiao)
had red [-boiled] strings and sparse holes [in the bottom],
and with one singing and three sighing,
there would be left-over music.
In the Ritual of the Great Ancestral Sacrifice,
water (lit. "black wine") was held highest
and raw fish was put on the offering stands;
the great thick-soup was not mixed [with spices, etc.], and there would be left-over flavors.
For this reason, the making of Ritual and Music by the former kings
was not in order to exhaust the desires of the mouth, the belly, the ears, and the eyes. I
t was used in order to instruct the people to level-out their likes and dislikes

and to return to the proper center of the Way of mankind.74 [Zheng Xuan says: "Lun IA is like lei M (classification). Li f means fen $} (divisions). 1.7 Man is born and is still --
this is Heaven's nature (xing).
[He is] touched off by [external] things and [only then] moves --
this is [his] nature's desires.
Things arrive and the [faculty of] knowledge apprehends [them] --
only then do likes and dislikes take shape therein.
If likes and dislikes have no regulation within
and the [faculty of] knowledge is enticed from without,
[man] can not return to [reflect upon] himself,
and the principles of Heaven (tianli R ) are destroyed.
Now if the touching off of man by things is without limit
and the likes and dislikes of man have no regulation,
then this is [a matter of] things arriving and men being transformed [by] things.
For man to be transformed [by] things
is to destroy the principles of Heaven and to extend human desires to the limit.
At that point there are rebellious and false hearts,
and there are licentious and havoc-wreaking affairs.
For this reason,
the many do violence to the few,
the powerful intimidate the weak,
the intelligent cheat the stupid,
and the courageous cause suffering to the cowardly.
Ailments and sicknesses are not convalesced, x
and the elderly, young, orphaned, and childless can not obtain their place.

This is the way of great chaos.80 [Zheng Xuan says: (After ".. . this is nature's desires") "This talks of how the nature does not have desires if it does not perceive things." 1.8 For this reason, the constructing of Ritual and Music by the former kings
[was a matter of] making regulation for the people.
The coarse hemp of mourning garments, crying and weeping --
these are what was used to regulate the mourning rites.
Bells and drums, shields and axes --
these are what was used to harmonize peace and happiness.
Marriages, caps and hairpins --
these are what was used to distinguish males and females.
Archery contests and celebrations, banquet entertainments --
these are what was used to engage in proper social intercourse.
Ritual regulates the people's hearts;
Music harmonizes the people's voices.
Administration is used to carry them out;
Punishment is used to prevent [transgressions against] them.

2. 樂論 The Discours of Music" 2.1 Music (yue) serves to unite (tong,
F[); Ritual cserves differentiate (yi, W).
With uniting there is mutual closeness;
differentiation there is mutual respect.
When Music gains the hand there is reckless abandon (liu L).
When Ritual gains the hand there is estrangement (li 0).
To unite (he -1) the emotions and to polish external appearances --
these are the affairs of and Music.
If the deportment of Ritual is established,
then the noble and the plebeian are separated into classes.
When the patterns of Music are uniform,
then those in high position and those in low position get along in harmony.
If likes and dislikes are made clear,
then the worthy and the unworthy are distinguished.
If punishments are used to prevent violence
and titles are used to esteem the worthy,
then the administration is on level ground.
Humanity (ren --) is used in loving them (the people)
and propriety (yi 4) is used in rectifying them --
if it is like this,

then the governance of the people will be implemented. [Zheng Xuan says: "Tong [ refers to harmonizing likes and dislikes. Yi qrefers to distinguishing between the worth and the lowly. Liu 'L refers to combined action without respect. Li irefers to living separately without harmony. [Of Ritual and Music] It is desired that they both be carried out, in a manner complete in both external refinement and internal qualities (binbinran M *i ,). Deng V are [social] classes.]
2.2 Music comes out from within,
Ritual comes into being from without.
Music comes out from within, thus it is still.
Ritual comes into being from without, thus it is ordered.
Great Music must be marked by ease,
Great Ritual must be marked by simplicity.90
If Music reaches the ultimate, there are no grievances.
If Ritual reaches the ultimate, [the people] do not struggle [with one another].
The governance of all under Heaven through deference
is what is meant by Ritual and Music.
Rebellious people do not arise,
the feudal lords submit like guests,
weaponry and armour are not employed,
and the five punishments are not made use of.
The masses are without suffering,
and the Son of Heaven is not angry. --
If it is like this,
then Music has reached its goal.
Uniting the affections of father and son,
making manifest the order of the old and the young,
so as to gain respect for the Son of Heaven throughout the land --
if it is like this,

then Ritual has been carried out. [Zheng Xuan says: "Harmony resides with the heart. Respect resides on the exterior. Wen :Z is like dong Mb (movement). Yi i (easy, peaceful) and jian f (simple), as with the qingmiao (odes to King Wen) and the Great Ancestral Sacrifice. Zhi - is like da i (to reach), xing I:T (to travel, be carried out). Bin - means xie S (to be in harmony, be united), Shi At means yong PJ (to use)"
2.3 Great Music shares in the harmony of Heaven and Earth.
Great Ritual shares in the regulation of Heaven and Earth.
There is harmony, thus the "hundred things" do not suffer loss;
there is regulation, thus [there are] sacrifices to Heaven and to Earth.
In the bright [sphere] there are Ritual and Music;
in the dark [sphere] there are ghosts and spirits.

throughout the land [the people]
